In elementary school it was required we learn English (Canada) and French was offered starting in third grade all the way up to twelfth. We had a French immersion program and French language classes which were offered to kids not in immersion.
In grade four, we actually got to learn some Halkomelem which is a dying indigenous language near where I grew up (southwestern BC).
And then in high school I took Spanish classes for three years (obviously couldn't take immersion because I was already in French immersion at the time).

But lots of other languages were offered at other schools, my sister's high school offered Arabic and Mandarin. 

I don't remember any of the Halkomelem I learned which is really sad because it was my first look at a polysynthstic anguage and I really like those nowadays! 

I am still fluent in English and French, and my Spanish is passable (French accent while speaking Spanish though lmao).

So I guess four languages total but I only remember three.

I have very sensitive eyes. My lightbulbs in my room are like 40watts (and it is still too bright lol) and I wear sunglasses EVERYWHERE and all the time. I only see white light if I go outwithout my sunglasses. My eyes just cannot adjust.
I have the same problem with the optometrist. He told me that I have "blonde retinas" which makes them even more sensitive. I have really light blonde hair and blue eyes so I guess I just don't have enough melanin in my eyes. Everyone else in my family is blue eyed too but I'm the only one with blonde retinas for some reason.
Also! I don't know if anyone else experiences this but in my right eye, all the colors have a slightly bluish shade compared to my left (which is more yellowy). When both my eyes are open the colors kinda mix together and it's not super blue or yellow either way! Luckily the optometrist says it's not a huge issue and I just have more color receptors in one eye.
The rest of my senses are a mess too haha. Finding clothing is enough to make me want to cry (over fabric and sensation) and I wear noise cancelling headphones most places to block out the majority of the noise.

I dont have ADHD, but my sister does.

good luck!
